To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

polyamines (PAS) application to maize seedlings under drought stress increased the tolerance of seedlings by modulating antioxidant and reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis, which resulted in higher pigment contents, reduced lipid peroxidation and increased photosynthetic pigments.
PAs application in drought condition increased the antioxidant effect in maize seedlings.

the application of PAs (Put, Spd and Spm) to maize seedlings under drought stress significantly increased tolerance and decreased ROS, lipid peroxidation, and MDA contents, while it increased proline, AsA and GSH contents and antioxidant enzymes activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of PAs on drought tolerance in maize seedlings.
the role of PAs on pigment content, ROS and antioxidant under drought in maize.
the role of polyamines (PAS) in the regulation of drought stress in maize.

polyamine application in maize seedlings increased drought tolerance by increasing antioxidant activity, decreasing ROS and MDA content and increasing total pigment content, while decreasing proline content.
PAs play a significant role in modulating the antioxidant system and ROS homeostasis under short term drought stress in maize seedlings.
PAs application in maize seedlings under short term drought significantly modulated the pigments, ROS, proline and antioxidant enzymes, and thus improved the tolerance.

PAs play important role in modulating the oxidative stress under drought by regulating the antioxidants and ROS.

the application of PAs can be used to increase tolerance to drought stress in maize.
